validity.researcher_notes: Same underlying evidence as the P5114/P6773 concerns, restated for Phase 3. DT Midstream's Aug 2023 investor presentation (https://s28.q4cdn.com/581450200/files/doc_presentations/2023/Aug/22/dtm-company-presentation-august-2023-vf.pdf, verified: contains 'LEAP') lists Phase 3 expansion (Q3 2024, +0.2 Bcf/d) on the same slide stating 'Project includes a combination of looping and compression' for the Phase 1-3 program overall, not compression alone. DT Midstream's FY2023 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1842022/000184202224000003/dtm-20231231.htm, verified: contains '209-mile') shows LEAP had already grown to 209 miles by Dec 31, 2023 (before Phase 3 was even placed in service), and DT Midstream's current asset page (https://dtmidstream.com/asset/leap-gathering-system/, verified: contains 'Gillis') now describes a 221-mile system after Phase 4 (2026) — a further ~12-mile increase since the FY2023 figure, consistent with continued new-pipe additions through Phase 3 and Phase 4. Oil & Gas Journal (https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/55240028/dt-midstream-expanding-haynesville-marcellus-natural-gas-pipeline-systems, verified: contains 'looping') independently describes DT Midstream's LEAP phase program (discussing the Phase 4 FID) as using 'incremental compression and looping.' This row's Capacity=200.00 MMcf/d matches the Phase 3 capacity figure (200 MMcf/d, 1.7->1.9 Bcf/d) reported across DT Midstream's investor materials and trade press covering the July 2024 Q2 earnings release ('Placed the LEAP Phase 3 expansion project in-service early and on budget' — https://investor.dtmidstream.com/investors/news/news-details/2024/DT-Midstream-Reports-Strong-Second-Quarter-2024-Results/default.aspx, verified: contains 'Phase 3'), confirming the row-to-phase match is correct. I found no Phase-3-specific mileage or diameter breakdown isolating this phase's share of the system's mileage growth, so I am not filling Diameter directly rather than risk a fabricated per-phase figure (standing rule 2).
